name: UA Client Hints, high entropy
plain: Detailed device and browser versions a site can request with Accept-CH or a JavaScript call.
meaning: Returns exact OS version, CPU, bitness, device model and full browser version. Not sent unless the site asks. The browser can decline, but Chrome currently answers without a prompt.

web.api: navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues([...]); Accept-CH response header then Sec-CH-UA-* request headers

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: model
fields.range: Android model such as Pixel 8, else empty

fields.name: formFactors
fields.range: Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, XR, Automotive, EInk, Watch

limits.headline: Can see detailed device and browser versions, but only if the site asks
limits.user_action: Nothing. The site asks and Chromium answers without a prompt
can: Get your exact OS version, chip, and 32 or 64 bit
Use the detail to serve the right app or ad
cannot: Work in Firefox, Safari, or on iPhone
Get anything until the site asks for it
See your name, location, or accounts
limits.differs: Chromium browsers answer without a prompt. Firefox and Safari do not offer these hints.

story.what_it_is: Detailed device and browser facts, like exact OS version and model, that a site can ask for.

marketing.name: User-Agent Client Hints
marketing.pitch: Chrome says sites should ask for only the detail they need, instead of getting everything by default.

story.for_you: You never see it. If a site asks, Chrome can hand over exact versions, chip type and device model. In return you get the right installer, the right layout or fewer bugs.
story.for_makers: The older user agent gave out everything. With hints, sites must ask, which gives the browser a chance to say no. Ad tech and fraud teams still ask for many hints, since together they are a rich device profile.

use_cases.example: A download page asks for CPU type and OS version to give the right installer.
A browser game asks for model and platform version to choose graphics settings that work on that device.
An ad exchange asks for full device details so bidders can target by model and OS version.
A bank asks for the full browser version to check it against known fakes.
A product team logs device model and OS version to prioritise fixes.
A streaming site asks for platform version to pick the right DRM level.
An IT dashboard reads exact versions to find outdated work laptops.

technical_bounds: Site must ask: header needs Accept-CH, JS call per hint
Delegation to third parties needs Permissions-Policy
Spec lets browsers refuse or lie; Chrome does not prompt today

abuse: Precise device fingerprint without any prompt
Targeting by exact model on Android

linkedin.how: user_agent_data source is part of mainstream fingerprint libraries; LinkedIn's list is mostly legacy navigator.* fields (not confirmed for getHighEntropyValues).

history.change: Becomes the only way to get OS minor version, arch, model after UA reduction
